subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - deployment-mode clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - deployment-mode clarifications

Hi Lina / team,

Thanks again for the demo today — great questions and useful context. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so we can size Dedicated correctly for your POC and eventual prod rollout. PTAL and reply inline where helpful.

Call recap (short):
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference for customer chat + long-form summarization pipelines; must serve US-only data.
- Deployment preference: evaluating Dedicated first (predictable throughput), with Private VPC as a potential requirement for audit/legal later.
- Compliance: SOC2 plus contractual data residency needed.

Sizing items we need from you to finalize a proposal: (if you don’t have exact numbers, ballpark is fine)
1) Peak and steady TPS (requests per second) and expected spike duration.
2) Average and 95th percentile token counts per request (prompt tokens vs generation tokens).
3) Concurrency targets/expected simultaneous users.
4) Latency SLOs (p50/p95) and whether p95 for chat must be sub-1s.
5) Any GPU preference (H100 vs A100) or budget constraints for instance types.

Attachments: I’ve attached the infra_requirements.xlsx we used in the call so you can fill the token mix and expected TPS columns. Also attaching a draft SLA we typically use for Dedicated pilots.

Next steps we propose: once we get the numbers above, Mateo will map to an initial GPU pool (recommendation + burst capacity plan) and we’ll provide a POC cost estimate and a short runbook. Can we get the TPS/token answers by EOD Thursday (Feb 19)?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - deployment-mode clarifications

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. See answers below (ballpark where noted). I’m copying Jordan from infra for any deeper perf numbers.

1) TPS (requests/sec): steady state 80 RPS during business hours. We see short spikes up to ~150 RPS that typically last 8–12 minutes when product campaigns run.
2) Token mix: average total tokens per request ~1,200 tokens. Rough split: prompt ~250 tokens, generation ~950 tokens. 95p is around 2,400 tokens during complex summarization jobs.
3) Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~60; we want headroom to 120 concurrent during spikes.
4) Latency SLO: p50 ~400ms, p95 target <= 1.2s for chat experiences. For async summarization jobs we can tolerate higher latencies but prefer throughput.
5) GPU preference/budget: we don’t have strict vendor requirement but Jordan suggests H100 would be preferred for our mix (longer context and FP16/TF32 workloads). Budget: mid-range — willing to commit to a POC-sized Dedicated pool but need pricing to evaluate.

Also, yes we will likely need a Private VPC option before full production due to customer contracts (US-only). SOC2 is also required.

I’ll try to get more precise token histograms from telemetry and share by Thursday.

— Lina
Lina Park | Head of Product Operations
StellarAI
lina.park@stellarai.com

Thanks Lina — these are very helpful numbers. Quick mapping from a runtime/sizing perspective and a couple of follow-up questions so the Dedicated proposal is right-sized.

Summary mapping (based on your averages and spikes):
- Steady 80 RPS, spikes to 150 RPS (8–12 min). Average request ~1,200 tokens, 95p ~2,400 tokens. Concurrency target 60, headroom 120.
- Model topology assumptions: 8k context models for summarization; generation-heavy workload.

Initial Dedicated recommendation (POC):
- GPU type: H100 80GB preferred for headroom on long-context runs and mixed precision workloads. H100 gives ~30–40 effective RPS per GPU at ~1,000–1,500 token lengths for our Llama-family + 8k context quantized stack (ballpark).
- Suggested baseline pool: 3x H100 for steady needs (3 * 35 RPS ~= 105 RPS effective) which covers steady 80 RPS with buffer.
- Autoscale/burst: allow burst to 6x H100 to cover spikes to 150 RPS and provide safety for retries/rehits. We can implement fast warm pools + KV prefix caching to reduce repeat token compute for similar prompts.
- Concurrency config: set per-GPU concurrency to 16–24 sessions with batching window tuned to 10–25ms. That maps to the cluster concurrency target near your 60–120 concurrent sessions.

Cost/throughput notes:
- If you can accept 4k context models or more aggressive quantization (int8), we can increase per-GPU throughput ~1.8x. We should prototype quantized weights on a sample production prompt set to validate quality.

Questions/asks:
1) Can you attach a sample of 50 anonymized requests (prompt + response sizes) so we can run a small local perf sweep and produce a validated RPS/GPU mapping? We’ll treat data as telemetry only; if needed we can sign an NDA for payloads.
2) Do you expect many long-running streaming sessions that require token-at-a-time latency guarantees (this matters for batching/burst configuration)?

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa collects the sample request set and the telemetry histograms Lina mentioned.
- I’ll create a POC configuration (3x H100 baseline + autoscale to 6x) + expected cost estimate and a simple runbook for hit patterns by Monday.

Attaching our SLA draft for reference.

--
Mateo Alvarez | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
